name: context-diet
description: The scale half of context-diet: keeps the standing tally of how much context each main-thread turn re-reads, where the turns sit, and which model your subagents ran on. Reads the live stream. Writes nothing, answers no agent, starts no process.

settings.label: Context cap to measure against
settings.description: Tokens. A turn above this is what the tally counts. 200,000 is where subagents already do real work, and it is the knee of the curve: capping there leaves 40% of the re-reading, capping at 500,000 leaves 79%.

settings.label: Largest context one turn can really have
settings.description: Tokens. A turn above this is a bookkeeping artefact rather than a turn: it is dropped and counted, never clamped. The count is drawn, so the guard cannot eat data quietly.

settings.label: Days of history to keep
settings.description: The tally covers this many days. Older turns are dropped from its own file on the next start.

settings.label: Read new turns every (seconds)
settings.description: There is no stream this can subscribe to without a WebSocket client, so it asks. Usage itself arrives 3 to 12 seconds late whatever this says, because it comes from the transcript scanner.
